name: Vada Pav
cuisine: Mumbai street food (Maharashtra; the format is credited to Ashok Vaidya, who started selling it outside Dadar station in 1966)

ingredients.name: Green chilli (hari mirch), for the filling
Kashmiri red chilli powder (lal mirch), for the batter
Coriander leaves (dhania), for chutney
ingredients.householdMeasure: a small handful (about ⅓ cup loosely packed)

ingredients.name: Dry garlic chutney (1 serving's share; make a 6× batch)
Kashmiri red chilli powder (lal mirch), for chutney
Green chilli (hari mirch), to fry and serve

equipment: Pressure cooker (2–3 litre) to boil the potatoes
Small kadai (deep wok), about 18–20 cm across, for deep-frying

No deep-frying (lower-oil alternatives): Appe pan (paniyaram pan): make smaller, bite-size vadas (about 25 g filling each, 6–7 per serving), dip them in the batter and cook in the cavities with ¼ tsp oil each on medium-low heat, covered, 3–4 min per side until golden
Slotted spoon (jhara) to lift the vadas
Small mixer jar (chutney jar) for both chutneys
Small pan for the tempering (the tawa or the kadai itself works)
Potato masher or a fork; mixing bowl for the batter; plate lined with kitchen paper (or a newspaper-free paper towel) to drain
Chopping board, knife, measuring spoons, serving plate

steps.title: Wash the potatoes
steps.text: Rinse 150 g potato (1 large or 2 small) under running water and scrub off any mud.
steps.visualCue: Clean skin, no soil in the eyes
steps.videoShot: Hands rubbing the potato under the tap.

steps.title: Pressure cook the potatoes
steps.text: Put the whole potatoes in the cooker with 150 ml (about ⅔ cup) water. Close and cook on medium heat for 3 whistles (about 10 min). Turn off the heat and let the pressure drop on its own.
steps.tip: Never force the lid open while there is still pressure.
steps.visualCue: 3 whistles; the float valve has dropped before you open the lid
steps.cameraCheck: The closed cooker on the stove
steps.videoShot: Steam puffing as the cooker whistles.

steps.title: Peel the chutney garlic
steps.text: Peel 2 cloves (6 g) garlic.
steps.visualCue: 2 clean, creamy-white cloves
steps.videoShot: The skin being slipped off a lightly crushed clove.

steps.title: Roast the peanuts
steps.text: Put a small pan on medium-low heat and dry roast 3 g (1 tsp) peanuts, stirring all the time.
steps.visualCue: Skins blister and crack; the peanuts smell nutty and have light brown spots
steps.cameraCheck: The roasted peanuts in the pan
steps.videoShot: Peanuts rolling around the hot pan.

steps.title: Roast the coconut
steps.text: Tip the peanuts onto a plate. In the same pan, dry roast 5 g (1 tbsp) desiccated coconut on low heat, stirring constantly.
steps.tip: Coconut burns in seconds once it starts to brown, so take it off the heat as soon as it is light golden.
steps.visualCue: Light golden-brown and toasty-smelling; not dark brown
steps.cameraCheck: The golden coconut in the pan
steps.videoShot: The spoon stirring the coconut as it colours.

steps.title: Fry the garlic
steps.text: Move the coconut to the plate. Add ½ tsp (2 g) oil to the pan and fry the 2 garlic cloves on low heat.
steps.visualCue: Light golden spots on the cloves; the sharp raw smell turns sweet and roasted
steps.videoShot: The cloves sizzling gently in the oil.

steps.title: Bloom the chilli powder
steps.text: Turn off the heat. Add ½ tsp (1.5 g) Kashmiri chilli powder to the hot pan and stir for 10 seconds.
steps.visualCue: The powder darkens slightly and smells toasty; it must not turn black
steps.cameraCheck: The red garlic mixture in the pan
steps.videoShot: The red powder hitting the oil and being stirred.

steps.title: Grind the dry chutney
steps.text: When everything is cool, put the peanuts, coconut, garlic with its chilli-oil and a tiny pinch of salt in the small mixer jar. Pulse in short bursts.
steps.tip: Grinding too long turns it into an oily paste. Stop while it is still crumbly.
steps.visualCue: A coarse, crumbly, red powder that looks like moist sand, not a paste
steps.cameraCheck: The dry chutney in the jar
steps.videoShot: The mixer pulsing and the red crumbs settling.

steps.title: Grind the green chutney
steps.text: Put 10 g coriander leaves (with tender stems), ½ green chilli (2 g), a few drops (2 ml) lemon juice, a tiny pinch of salt and 2 tsp water in the same jar (no need to wash it). Grind smooth, adding 1 more tsp water if needed.
steps.visualCue: A bright green, smooth, spreadable sauce that slowly drips off a spoon
steps.cameraCheck: The green chutney in a small bowl
steps.videoShot: The green chutney being scraped out of the jar.

steps.title: Peel and mash the potatoes
steps.text: Open the cooker, peel the potatoes while warm and mash them in a bowl with a masher or fork.
steps.tip: If the potato is watery, leave the mash uncovered for 5 min so steam escapes. Wet filling makes the batter slide off.
steps.visualCue: Mostly smooth with a few small pea-sized lumps; no water pooling
steps.cameraCheck: The mashed potato in the bowl
steps.videoShot: The masher pressing down on the potato.

steps.title: Crush the garlic, ginger and chilli
steps.text: Peel 2 cloves (6 g) garlic and ½ inch (3 g) ginger. Crush them with 1 green chilli (4 g) to a coarse paste in a mortar and pestle (or chop very finely).
steps.visualCue: A coarse, pale-green paste with small bits
steps.videoShot: The pestle pounding the garlic, ginger and chilli.

steps.title: Chop the coriander
steps.text: Finely chop 5 g (1 heaped tbsp) coriander leaves for the filling.
steps.visualCue: Fine green flecks
steps.videoShot: The knife rocking through the coriander.

steps.title: Heat the tempering oil
steps.text: Put the small pan on medium heat with 1 tsp (5 g) oil.
steps.visualCue: The oil shimmers and flows easily
steps.videoShot: Oil swirling in the pan.

steps.title: Splutter the mustard seeds
steps.text: Add ⅛ tsp (0.5 g) mustard seeds.
steps.visualCue: The seeds pop and crackle and turn grey
steps.cameraCheck: The popping seeds in the pan
steps.videoShot: Mustard seeds jumping in the oil.

steps.title: Add hing and curry leaves
steps.text: Add a small pinch of asafoetida and 5–6 curry leaves (torn).
steps.tip: Curry leaves spit when they hit hot oil. Stand back a little.
steps.visualCue: A loud sizzle; the leaves turn darker and glossy
steps.cameraCheck: The curry leaves in the oil
steps.videoShot: Curry leaves crackling.

steps.title: Fry the garlic-ginger-chilli paste
steps.text: Add the paste from step 11 and stir on low-medium heat.
steps.visualCue: The raw garlic smell turns mellow; the paste is lightly golden at the edges
steps.videoShot: The spoon stirring the paste in the tempering.

steps.title: Add turmeric
steps.text: Add a pinch (0.3 g) turmeric and stir for 5 seconds, then turn off the heat.
steps.visualCue: The oil turns bright yellow
steps.videoShot: Turmeric swirling into the oil.

steps.title: Mix the filling
steps.text: Pour the tempering over the mashed potato. Add ¼ tsp (1.5 g) salt, 1 tsp (5 ml) lemon juice and the chopped coriander. Mix well with a spoon.
steps.tip: Taste now. The filling should taste a little saltier and spicier than you like, because the batter and pav are bland.
steps.visualCue: An even, pale-yellow mix with green and dark specks spread throughout
steps.cameraCheck: The finished filling in the bowl
steps.videoShot: The yellow tempering being folded into the potato.

steps.title: Shape the vadas
steps.text: Divide the filling into 2 equal parts (about 85 g each). Roll each into a ball between your palms, then flatten slightly into a thick disc about 6 cm across and 2.5 cm thick.
steps.tip: Slightly flattened balls fit inside a pav better and cook through evenly.
steps.visualCue: 2 smooth, crack-free discs about the size of a small lemon
steps.cameraCheck: The 2 shaped vadas on a plate
steps.videoShot: Palms rolling and lightly pressing a ball.

steps.title: Mix the dry batter ingredients
steps.text: In a bowl, put 30 g (3½ tbsp) gram flour, 3 g (1 tsp) rice flour, a tiny pinch of turmeric, a small pinch (0.5 g) Kashmiri chilli powder, a pinch of salt and a tiny pinch (0.2 g) of baking soda. Stir to mix.
steps.visualCue: An even, pale-yellow powder with no white streaks of rice flour
steps.cameraCheck: The dry mix in the bowl
steps.videoShot: A spoon stirring the dry flours.

steps.title: Add water and whisk
steps.text: Add 35 ml (about 2½ tbsp) water, a little at a time, whisking with a spoon or small whisk until there are no lumps. Add up to 5 ml (1 tsp) more water only if needed.
steps.tip: Too thin and the coating slips off; too thick and it turns doughy. Thicker is safer than thinner.
steps.visualCue: A smooth batter that coats the back of a spoon in a thick, even layer and falls in a slow ribbon, like thick pancake batter
steps.videoShot: The batter ribboning off the spoon back into the bowl.

steps.title: Heat the frying oil
steps.text: Pour 250–300 ml oil into a small kadai (about 4–5 cm deep) and heat on medium-high.
steps.tip: If the test drop stays at the bottom, the oil is too cool and the vada will soak up oil. If it browns instantly, lower the heat.
steps.visualCue: About 170–180°C. A drop of batter sinks slightly, then rises to the top within 2–3 seconds with steady bubbles
steps.cameraCheck: The test drop of batter floating in the oil
steps.videoShot: The test drop rising and sizzling.

steps.title: Coat the first vada
steps.text: Drop one vada into the batter and turn it with a spoon (or your fingers) until fully covered, with no potato showing.
steps.visualCue: A smooth, even, yellow coat all over
steps.cameraCheck: The coated vada lifted over the bowl
steps.videoShot: The vada being turned in the batter.

steps.title: Slide it into the oil
steps.text: Gently lower the coated vada into the oil from close to the surface (about 2 cm). Coat and add the second vada the same way.
steps.tip: Lower it with your fingertips close to the oil, never drop it from a height, so hot oil does not splash.
steps.visualCue: Immediate, lively bubbling all around the vada
steps.videoShot: The vada sliding into the oil and the bubbles rising.

steps.title: Let the coating set
steps.text: Leave the vadas untouched on medium heat so the batter firms up.
steps.visualCue: The coating looks firm and pale gold underneath; the vada floats
steps.videoShot: The vadas bobbing in the bubbling oil.

steps.title: Turn and fry until golden
steps.text: Turn each vada gently with the slotted spoon and keep frying on medium heat, turning every 30–45 sec.
steps.visualCue: Even golden-brown all over; the bubbling slows down and the sizzle becomes quieter (most of the moisture in the coating has cooked off)
steps.cameraCheck: A vada held up on the slotted spoon
steps.videoShot: The slotted spoon turning a golden vada.

steps.title: Drain the vadas
steps.text: Lift each vada out, hold it over the kadai for 5 seconds to drip, then place it on a plate lined with kitchen paper.
steps.visualCue: Crisp, golden, with only a small oil mark on the paper
steps.videoShot: The vada lifted and dripping over the kadai.

steps.title: Make the fried chillies
steps.text: Slit 2 green chillies (8 g) lengthwise once, leaving the stems on. Pat them dry. Carefully slide them into the same oil.
steps.tip: Wet chillies spit a lot. Dry them well and stand back, or cover the kadai partly with a lid.
steps.visualCue: The skin blisters and turns pale green with white patches
steps.cameraCheck: The blistered chillies in the oil
steps.videoShot: The chillies blistering in the oil.

steps.title: Salt the chillies
steps.text: Lift out the chillies onto the paper and sprinkle a tiny pinch of salt over them. Turn off the heat under the oil.
steps.tip: Drizzle any leftover batter through the slotted spoon into the oil for 30–40 sec to make crisp fried drops (chura) before turning off the heat. Not counted in nutrition.
steps.visualCue: Glossy, blistered chillies with a few salt crystals
steps.videoShot: Salt falling on the chillies.

steps.title: Slit the pav
steps.text: Cut 2 pav through the middle horizontally, leaving one side joined like a book.
steps.tip: Optionally warm the pav on a dry tawa for 20 sec per side; street stalls usually serve it untoasted.
steps.visualCue: Each pav opens flat like a book
steps.videoShot: The knife sliding through a pav.

steps.title: Spread the green chutney
steps.text: Spread about 1 tsp green chutney on the inside of each pav (both halves).
steps.visualCue: A thin, even green layer on both cut sides
steps.videoShot: The spoon spreading the chutney.

steps.title: Sprinkle the dry garlic chutney
steps.text: Sprinkle about ½ tbsp dry garlic chutney over the green chutney in each pav.
steps.visualCue: Red crumbs sticking all over the green layer
steps.videoShot: Red chutney being sprinkled from a spoon.

steps.title: Add the vada and press
steps.text: Place a hot vada in each pav, close it and press gently so the vada cracks slightly and the chutneys stick.
steps.visualCue: The pav closes around the vada with a golden edge peeking out
steps.videoShot: A palm pressing the pav shut.

steps.title: Plate it
steps.text: Put the 2 vada pav and the 2 salted fried chillies on a plate, with any leftover dry chutney on the side.
steps.visualCue: 2 vada pav with green and red chutney showing, and 2 blistered chillies alongside
steps.videoShot: A slow pan over the plate, then a hand breaking one vada pav open.

reasons: the batata vada is deep-fried (about 34 g fat in the serving, most of it from frying and the oil-rich garlic chutney), the pav is refined flour, and sodium is high (about 1,450 mg). On the plus side, besan adds some protein and fibre (about 21 g protein and 11 g fibre in total), the chutneys add coriander and garlic, and at home you control fresh oil and salt. Street versions are usually fried in oil that is reused through the day (which can build up harmful oxidation products), may use palm oil, and are often eaten as 2–3 pieces with sweet chutney or butter.

researchRating.basis: vada pav is Mumbai's best-known street snack, widely called the "Bombay burger" and eaten across income groups. Top home recipes score almost perfectly (snippets showed Hebbar's Kitchen 4.98 from 362 votes and Indian Healthy Recipes 5 from 104 votes), Ashok Vada Pav in Dadar was placed 25th on TasteAtlas's list of the world's most iconic sandwiches, and food media list many must-visit stalls (Ashok, Graduate, Anand, Gajanan). It is a little short of 5 because it is widely seen as a cheap, deep-fried, carb-heavy snack rather than a meal, and home versions rarely match the street-stall texture.

storage: An assembled vada pav does not keep well (the pav goes soggy), so assemble only what you will eat. Leftover plain vadas keep in the fridge for 1–2 days in an airtight box; uncooked potato filling keeps 2 days. Fried vadas can be frozen for up to 1 month. Reheat vadas in an air fryer at 180°C for 4–5 min, or in a dry pan on low heat, covered, for 6–8 min, turning often, until crisp again (the microwave makes them soft and chewy). Green chutney keeps 2–3 days in the fridge; dry garlic chutney keeps about 1 month in an airtight jar at room temperature, or 2–3 months in the fridge. Keep pav at room temperature (1–2 days).
leftoverRemix: Vada ragda chaat. Break 1–2 leftover vadas into chunks on a plate, warm them, then top with 3 tbsp warm boiled white peas or chana (or leftover dal), 1 tbsp chopped onion, 1 tbsp curd, a spoon each of green and tamarind chutney, a pinch of chaat masala and a handful of sev. It is a quick take on Mumbai's "vada usal" and "samosa ragda" plates.
burnOff: about 10.5 km of running (746 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 15 km of brisk walking (about 3 hours at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).
